title: Topical 3% tranexamic acid and fine lines: an exploratory wrinkle result from a melasma trial, plus a cell-culture mechanism
headline: In 50 women with melasma, a 3% tranexamic acid serum was followed by a small drop in periorbital wrinkle score versus moisturizer alone; the wrinkle result was not the trial's planned outcome, and the mechanism comes from fibroblasts in a dish.
evidenceTier: Exploratory secondary analysis of an RCT (open label as far as stated) plus in-vitro work; full text read
fit: Pigment-prone skin: Partial. Tranexamic acid is already a pigment-lane ingredient; the new part is a possible fine-line side benefit that has not been confirmed.
displaces: Nothing new. If a tranexamic acid serum is already in the pigment step, this adds a reason to keep it, not a reason to add a step.
regions: Global (cosmetic serums; concentration and claims vary by country)
Rx tranexamic acid tablets differ by country and are a separate question
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Tranexamic acid serums are widely marketed; I did not price any, so I cannot say whether price tracks this evidence. The evidence here is thin for a wrinkle claim.
summaryPoints: Observation (full text read): 50 women with melasma, phototypes III to V (about 78% IV), were randomised 1:1 to 3% tranexamic acid serum plus moisturizer or moisturizer alone, twice daily for 8 weeks, followed to week 12. All 50 completed.

Observation: periorbital wrinkle score (modified Fitzpatrick scale, graded blind by two dermatologists) changed by -0.43 vs +0.03 at week 12 (p<0.001). Baseline scores were low (about 1.4 to 1.6), so this is early fine lines, not deep wrinkles.
Observation: the wrinkle analysis was post hoc. The authors say they noticed it during a melasma trial. The melasma trial itself is a separate paper that I did not open.

Inference: the cell work (D-galactose-aged fibroblasts at 200 ug/mL, GPR30 blocking and knockdown, docking) is mechanistic support at best; D-galactose senescence is a lab model and 200 ug/mL is not a skin concentration.
Limits: single hospital, no vehicle-matched serum (control was moisturizer only), no blinding statement for participants, no collagen measurement.
toneData: Fitzpatrick III to V (III 18%, IV 78%, V 4%); Chinese women, 18 to 60
fitLine: Low-risk cosmetic ingredient with a plausible but unconfirmed fine-line side benefit; worth noticing, not worth buying for.
timeline: Wrinkle change appeared from week 4 and was largest at weeks 8 to 12 in the trial; no data past week 12

fitAxes.why: Barrier function and irritation were not reported in the text I read.
Other anti-wrinkle products and procedures were prohibited during the trial, so use with a retinoid is untested.
Pigment-lane ingredient; daily SPF is standard alongside it, though not stated as a protocol element here.

dossier.whatItIs: Tranexamic acid is a lysine-analogue originally used to reduce bleeding. Topical and oral forms are used for melasma. This paper reports an unplanned look at periorbital fine lines in the trial arm that used a 3% serum, and adds fibroblast experiments.

steps: Applied: 3% tranexamic acid serum twice daily on the face for 8 weeks (human trial).

Stated by the authors: tranexamic acid raised GPR30 levels and lowered MAPK phosphorylation in D-galactose-stressed fibroblasts, with fewer senescence markers (SA-beta-gal, p16, p21) and lower IL-6, IL-8, MMP1 and MMP3 expression.
Cell evidence: blocking GPR30 with G15 or knocking it down weakened these effects, which supports GPR30 involvement in that model.
Inferred, not shown: that the same pathway operates in living human dermis at topical doses and explains the wrinkle score change. No collagen, elastin or skin biopsy data were collected.
mechanism.inferenceFlag: The step from fibroblast culture to the wrinkle score is the authors' hypothesis. The human result and the cell result were not linked by any measurement in the same people.
mechanism.diagramCaption: Applied serum -> (hypothesis) GPR30-dependent lowering of MAPK and inflammatory signals in dermal fibroblasts -> (measured) lower early periorbital wrinkle score by week 8 to 12.

flow.label: Lower senescence and matrix-degrading signals
flow.note: p16, p21, IL-6, IL-8, MMP1, MMP3 measured in culture only.

flow.label: Lower periorbital wrinkle score
flow.note: -0.43 vs +0.03 on a low-baseline scale at week 12; post hoc.

studies.cite: Lin Y, Wang Y, Wang W, et al. Tranexamic acid protects human dermal fibroblasts from D-galactose-induced senescence via the GPR30/MAPK pathway. Ann Med 2026;58(1):2663263.
studies.design: Exploratory analysis of a randomised, moisturizer-controlled trial (Xiangya Hospital, China, June to December 2021), 1:1, 25 per arm; plus fibroblast experiments (primary cells from circumcised foreskin of donors aged 5 to 20).
studies.who: Women 18 to 60 with facial melasma, phototypes II to IV by protocol (III to V enrolled); excluded thromboembolic disease, anticoagulants, pregnancy, and use of other depigmenting or anti-wrinkle products. Mean age 36.7.
results: Inter-rater agreement between the two graders was high (ICC 0.89 to 0.92).
Cell results: lower ROS and MDA, higher SOD and catalase activity with tranexamic acid; effects reduced by GPR30 blocking or knockdown.
studies.effectSize: About 0.4 scale points on a scale whose baseline here was about 1.5; the paper does not give a minimal clinically important difference.
studies.placebo: Control was moisturizer alone, so the serum vehicle was not matched. The control group returned to baseline by week 12, which is what a stable no-effect arm looks like.
studies.material: Unclear. A 0.4-point change on a low-baseline grading scale is visible to blinded graders but I cannot say it is noticeable to the wearer; no patient-rated outcome is reported.
studies.adverse: Not reported in the text I read.
studies.conflict: No funding or conflict statement located in the text I read; check the front matter.
studies.limits: Post hoc analysis of a trial built for melasma; unblinded participants likely (serum vs none); one centre; no biopsy or collagen data; fibroblasts from young male donors and an artificial ageing model.

claimsCheck.claim: Tranexamic acid is an anti-ageing ingredient
claimsCheck.source: Authors' conclusion and likely brand marketing
claimsCheck.status: One exploratory trial analysis (n=50) plus a lab model; not an established anti-ageing effect.

claimsCheck.source: Cell experiments with an antagonist and knockdown
claimsCheck.status: Supported in the dish only; docking energy of -5.4 kcal/mol is a computational suggestion, not binding data.

products.rankNote: No product is named in the paper and I did not open any retailer or brand page this run, so no product is recommended or priced. Check any tranexamic acid serum's label for the actual percentage; the trial used 3%.

items.name: Tranexamic acid serums (category)
items.note: Concentrations vary on the market; the tested concentration was 3%.

howToUse: This is not a reason to add a product. If a tranexamic acid serum is already in the pigment step, the trial used it twice daily on the whole face for 8 weeks.
The trial prohibited other anti-wrinkle products during the study, so any layering with retinoids or acids is outside the evidence.

expect.what: In the trial the gap versus moisturizer opened by week 4 and was largest by week 8.
Benefit persisted 4 weeks after stopping in this trial; longer follow-up is not available.

dossier.contraindications: Trial exclusions for the topical arm: history of thromboembolic disease or clotting disorders, anticoagulant use, pregnancy or lactation, known hypersensitivity. Topical absorption is low but the trial did not measure it; ask a clinician if any of those apply.
dossier.sideBenefits: The melasma effect is the established reason people use it; this paper adds only the exploratory fine-line signal.
wouldChangeVerdict: A planned, blinded trial with fine lines as the primary outcome and a vehicle-matched serum
A study that includes phototypes V and VI and reports patient-rated change
Skin biopsy or ultrasound data showing dermal change in people
dossier.transfer: Does it transfer to deeper skin? Phototypes III to V were enrolled (78% type IV, 4% type V) and none of type VI, so deep skin is thinly represented. The pigment pathways are not tone-specific, so a similar effect is plausible by mechanism, but that is inference. Fine-line grading scales are also less validated on deeper skin.
confidence: Read in full: Lin 2026 (open-access full text).
Not opened: the original melasma trial this analysis came from; no product pages; no price data.
Unknown: funding, adverse events, blinding of participants.
